_meta.purpose: Bank-specific MSME CC/OD lending benchmarks for FinsightOne traffic light analysis. Used by Module 3A of the Master Prompt Library.
_meta.usage: In n8n, match client's primary_bank field to a key below and pass the object as {{bank_benchmarks_json}} to the Claude prompt.
_meta.fallback_logic: If bank not found: use PSU_DEFAULT for govt banks, PRIVATE_DEFAULT for private banks, NBFC_DEFAULT for NBFCs.

enhancement_timing.reason: PSU banks do limit reviews post-quarter. March and September are balance sheet driven — they are conservative then.

PSU_DEFAULT.dp_formula: 75% of stock (as per latest stock statement) + 75% of debtors under 90 days − creditors
PSU_DEFAULT.credit_culture: Conservative. Relationship-driven. Weight repayment track record and ITR consistency above all else. Slow approval cycles (4–8 weeks). Respond well to routing more business through their account.

enhancement_timing.reason: Private banks operate on calendar-year targets. H1 and post-July are hungry for good MSME book growth.

PRIVATE_DEFAULT.dp_formula: 75% of stock + 80% of debtors under 90 days − creditors (some private banks use 80% for debtors)
PRIVATE_DEFAULT.credit_culture: More aggressive. Score-driven. Faster approvals (1–3 weeks for clean files). Less relationship-weight, more data-weight. Bureau score and CC utilisation pattern are automated flags.

enhancement_timing.reason: NBFCs are targets-driven year round. Timing matters less than file quality.

NBFC_DEFAULT.dp_formula: 70% of stock + 70% of debtors under 120 days − creditors (varies widely by NBFC)
NBFC_DEFAULT.credit_culture: Flexible on collateral and financials. Higher rates compensate for risk. Faster but more expensive. Good for MSMEs who cannot get PSU/private bank approval. Do not stay with NBFC long-term if bank options exist.

enhancement_timing.reason: SBI does MSME limit reviews post-half-year. Credit managers have fresh targets in April and October.

SBI.processing_route: Limits above ₹25L go through MSME processing centre. Branch RM recommends; credit centre approves. Relationship with branch RM is key — they draft the internal note.
SBI.credit_culture: Most conservative of all PSU banks. Heavy weight on ITR consistency, DSCR, and zero cheque returns. Respond strongly to routing all primary transactions through SBI. Processing time: 4–8 weeks for clean files.
enhancement_docs_required: Stock statement as of last month-end
SBI.dp_formula: 75% of paid stock + 75% of debtors under 90 days − all creditors
SBI.negotiation_note: SBI rates are MCLR-linked. Negotiation is possible at renewal for scores above 720. Route all transactions through SBI and mention it explicitly — branch credit managers are told to reward primary account relationships.
common_rejection_reasons: ITR income inconsistent with bank credits

Bank of Baroda.processing_route: MSME limits processed at Baroda MSME Sulabh branches. Faster than SBI for documented files.
Bank of Baroda.credit_culture: Moderately conservative. Slightly more open than SBI on DSCR thresholds. Active MSME book growth target. Processing time: 3–6 weeks.
Bank of Baroda.dp_formula: 75% of stock + 75% of debtors under 90 days − creditors
Bank of Baroda.negotiation_note: BoB has been competitive on MSME rates to gain book share. Negotiation possible for bureau score above 715.

Punjab National Bank.credit_culture: Conservative. Slower processing than BoB. Strong relationship with North India MSME sector. Branch manager has more discretion than SBI.

Canara Bank.credit_culture: Strong in South India MSME sector. Moderately conservative. Good for manufacturing MSMEs.

enhancement_timing.reason: HDFC runs half-yearly MSME book reviews. Relationship managers have fresh enhancement targets in Jan and July.

HDFC Bank.processing_route: Most MSME CC/OD processed at branch level up to ₹5Cr. Above ₹5Cr goes to regional credit. Fast for clean files — 5–10 business days.
HDFC Bank.credit_culture: Data-driven. Automated bureau and utilisation triggers. CC utilisation above 80% gets auto-flagged for closer monitoring. Bureau score below 700 rarely gets manual override. Faster but less forgiving on bureau.
HDFC Bank.dp_formula: 80% of stock + 80% of debtors under 90 days − creditors
HDFC Bank.negotiation_note: HDFC negotiates on rate for bureau 720+ clients. They respond to competitor rate quotes — especially from ICICI and Axis. Mention the competitor rate calmly, not as a threat.
common_rejection_reasons: CC utilisation above 85% at review date
Any cheque return in prior 6 months

ICICI Bank.processing_route: ICICI iMobile and digital-first for smaller limits. Above ₹2Cr — relationship manager driven. Fast digital processing for clean files.
ICICI Bank.credit_culture: Most aggressive of large private banks for MSME acquisition. Willing to match competitor rates. Strong digital bureau integration — bureau flags are instant. Good for growing MSME businesses with strong GST data.
ICICI Bank.dp_formula: 75% of stock + 80% of debtors under 90 days − creditors
ICICI Bank.negotiation_note: ICICI is the most negotiation-friendly on rates. They actively compete with HDFC. Bureau 720+ with clean utilisation can get 10.75–11.25%.

Axis Bank.processing_route: SME Business Banking vertical. Dedicated SME RM for limits above ₹1Cr. Processing 7–14 days.
Axis Bank.credit_culture: Balanced between data-driven and relationship. More flexible than HDFC on DSCR thresholds for established customers. Responds well to long banking vintage.
Axis Bank.dp_formula: 75% of stock + 75% of debtors under 90 days − creditors
Axis Bank.negotiation_note: Axis responds to vintage-based loyalty arguments. 5+ year customers with clean record can get 0.25–0.50% below standard rate.

Kotak Mahindra Bank.credit_culture: Conservative for a private bank. Higher bureau score expectation. Good for high-income professional MSME owners. Selective about sectors.
Kotak Mahindra Bank.dp_formula: 75% of stock + 75% of debtors under 90 days − creditors
Kotak Mahindra Bank.negotiation_note: Less negotiation-friendly than ICICI/HDFC. Kotak maintains standard rates and rarely moves on price.

IndusInd Bank.credit_culture: Aggressive MSME growth targets. More flexible on bureau and collateral than HDFC/ICICI. Good option for businesses needing faster approval or with slightly lower scores.

IDFC First Bank.credit_culture: Growth-oriented. Competitive on digital MSME products. Less history than older banks — more flexible on criteria but slightly higher rates.

Yes Bank.credit_culture: Rebuilding MSME book post-2020 crisis. Stricter on documentation. Slightly higher rates. Relationship manager quality varies by branch.
Yes Bank.analyst_note: Advise clients to keep Yes Bank as secondary bank only. Do not recommend building primary banking relationship with Yes Bank currently.

Bajaj Finance.credit_culture: Fully digital underwriting. Fast (24–72 hours). High rates. Good for bridge finance or clients who cannot get bank approval. Advise to refinance to bank CC within 12–18 months.
Bajaj Finance.analyst_note: Bajaj Finance CC is a last resort for MSME clients. Rates are 4–6% above PSU banks. Always recommend moving to bank product if possible.

Tata Capital.credit_culture: More conservative than Bajaj. Tata brand brings better underwriting standards. Suitable for larger MSME working capital where banks are slow.

Ugro Capital.credit_culture: Sector-focused NBFC. Specialises in 8 MSME sectors. Uses GST data heavily for underwriting. Good for newer businesses with thin ITR history.

Lendingkart.credit_culture: Digital-only. Cash flow-based underwriting from bank statements and GST. No physical documents needed. Very fast (hours). Very expensive. Only for urgent bridge needs.
Lendingkart.analyst_note: Lendingkart rates are very high. Only recommend if client has exhausted all bank options and needs funds urgently. Always pair with a plan to refinance.

_market_rates_june_2026._note: Current market CC/OD rates for MSME clients with bureau score 700–750, 3+ year vintage, clean repayment. Updated June 2026. Used by Module 4C (Rate Negotiation Brief).
